1b.look.units.topic: check that the quantity, its unit and the weight agree before any price
hints: Compare what the quantity says with what the scale says.
Work out the weight each line should have from its quantity and unit, then divide the declared weight by it.
Join the tariff on hs8, compare unit with the code's unit, and look at net_kg / (quantity x kg_per_unit).

1b.look.data_clean.topic: check the six fields that decide whether anything downstream can be computed
hints: Six fields decide whether the rest is computable.
Count blanks and impossible values in each of the six fields.
tin_customs blank share; unit against tariff; description near-empty; outcome null share by half.

1b.signals.peer_group.topic: compare with the typical value for the same goods from the same origin over the last 12 months; widen the group when it has too few lines
hints: Some goods and origins are too rare to have a fair comparison group.
For each line count the peers at each level and note the first level with enough lines.
Use peer_level_used and peer_n_used; the deck's cell is the phone code from the biggest origin over the last twelve months.

1b.signals.price.topic: compare value per kilo with the typical value for the same goods and origin, using the median not the average
hints: Look for importers who are low again and again, not once.
Compute each line's distance from the typical value and the share of each importer's lines beyond the cut.
Share of lines with robust_z below minus three per importer_id, among importers with fifteen lines or more; read the discount importer as the decoy.

1b.signals.tenure.topic: look at how long each importer has been known and how much it already imports
hints: Newcomers that grow very fast deserve a second look.
Compute months since registration and the 12-month import value for every importer.
Filter tenure_months below twelve and sort by value_12m_lcu.

1b.signals.code_drift.topic: watch the share of an importer's lines that move to the cheapest code of a heading, month after month
hints: Some importers change their habits slowly, and a broker can be the hand that moves them.
For each importer and broker, compare the recent share of lines under the cheapest code with the share before.
Sort importer-broker pairs by code_drift_score; the pair that tops the list did it over the first half's second quarter.

1b.signals.description.topic: read the goods description and ask which code it really sounds like
hints: The words on the declaration can disagree with the code.
Score each line for 'sounds like another code' and read the top lines against their declared codes.
Sort by text_code_disagreement with text_higher_duty; then group the disagreements by office to see the data-quality office.

1b.signals.origin.topic: check that the claimed origin makes the goods, and how many importers each seller serves
hints: A preference needs an origin that can make the goods.
Flag preference claims from origins that do not produce the goods, then count importers per seller.
Compare origin with tariff.origin_producers; group the doubtful claims by exporter_id; watch exporter_importers_12m.

1b.signals.history.topic: look at how often each importer's declarations are amended or withdrawn
hints: How often does an importer change its mind?
Compute the share of each importer's lines amended or withdrawn.
Leave out lines amended after a finding; group by importer_id; sort.

1b.ladder.rule.topic: rule: inspect the lines priced below the old reference
hints: The simplest rule is a price cut-off.
Write the rule, count what it flags, and read the outcome only on the random draw.
Apply R2 to months 19-36 random lines; precision falls below 15%: the reference is stale.

1b.ladder.distance.topic: measure how far a line is from normal, both against peers and against the importer's own past
hints: A line can be normal for everyone else and odd for this importer.
Compute the distance of each line from the importer's own typical value for the same goods.
Own-history z for lines from month twenty-nine against the same importer's earlier lines in the same code; keep lines near the peer median and sort by z, lowest first.

1b.ladder.oddness.topic: an oddness score that looks at all signals together
hints: A line that is a little odd on two counts can matter more than one very odd on one.
Score all signals together and read the top lines.
Sort by oddness_score; compare with the single-signal rankings.

1b.ladder.learning.topic: a score learned from past inspection results
hints: A model only learns from the lines someone chose to inspect.
Train on controlled lines, compare hit rates at the same budget on the random draw, then retrain on red-lane lines only.
Use learned_score and learned_score_red_only on random_draw = 1 lines of months 19-36; top 5% by each; read the hit rate.

1b.ladder.expiry.topic: watch a rule's hit rate month by month after it was written
hints: A rule ages.
Compute the hit rate of the rule for each month of the second half, on the random draw only.
Group random-draw lines by period_month; compare months nineteen to twenty-four with thirty-one to thirty-six.

1b.newidea.clustering.topic: find the groups inside one tariff line, then the line that fits none of them
hints: One tariff line can hold two very different products.
Plot value per kilo against weight per unit and let the machine find two groups.
k=2 on usd_per_kg and kg_per_unit; sort by distance_to_nearest_group.

1b.newidea.timeseries.topic: compare each month with the importer's own past
hints: An importer can drift while its peers stay put.
Build each importer's band from its earlier months and flag months below it.
Find the first month below the band in the last year; overlay the reference median to tell an importer's drop from a market's drop.

1b.exercise.topic: weigh the signals, rank the twenty lines, pick five with a reason each
hints: Not every low price is a finding.
Weigh price, description, weight and origin, then check each pick for a units or own-history explanation.
Price alone catches the two decoys; add description and weight, then drop the wrong unit and the discount.

2b.valuation.neighbours.topic: find what similar goods were accepted at, put every price on one basis, and read the middle half
hints: Which fields make two descriptions similar?
How many neighbours is enough?
The range is never a value.

2b.mirror.bridge.topic: start from the partner's exports, add shipping and insurance, subtract each known explanation; what is left is worth a query
hints: The partner's books are a second witness.
Add shipping-and-insurance to the partner's exports, then add back timing and hub goods to what home recorded.
Chapter thirty-nine from the first partner, latest year: the wedge is eight percent.

2b.mirror.regional_uv.topic: compare the price Country A pays with the regional median for the same goods from the same seller, on two rulers
hints: Neighbours buy the same goods from the same sellers.
Divide Country A's value per kilo by the median of the ten importers for the same goods, seller and year, on each ruler.
uv_ratio for importer = Country A below the threshold; check reported_weight_share.

2b.mirror.sector_heatmap.topic: read the chapter-by-country map: a column is one country's audit map, a row a sector worth a regional conversation
hints: A map of the region shows where to look first.
Colour each chapter-country cell by its ratio to the regional median and read Country A's column, skipping the greyed cells.
In Country A's column list the chapters below the threshold; in each row count the countries below it.

2b.series.shapes.topic: read each corridor's eight years: always low, one bad year, new, or normal
hints: A gap has a shape.
Plot the adjusted ratio over the years for each corridor and apply the simple rules.
persistent: every year below 0.80; spike: one year far below the others; new: zero before the last two years.

2b.segments.topic: group importers by their signals, then read the control record of each group
hints: A clean record can hide a risky group.
Segment importers on the trader signals, then read the hit rate of each segment on the first half.
Use importer_cluster; read hit_rate_h1 by cluster; the top cluster is small and mostly one type.

2b.brokers.scorecard.topic: score brokers on what happens to their clients
hints: Brokers concentrate risk.
For each broker, compute the share of its clients that had a finding.
Sort by broker_flagged_share_h1 among brokers with at least five clients.

2b.network.hub.topic: find the sellers connected to the most importers
hints: Some sellers sit in the middle of everything.
Count each seller's links to importers.
Sort exporters by degree.

2b.regimes.warehouse.topic: check that what went in minus what came out equals the stock declared
hints: Stock should balance.
Opening stock plus entries minus exits, minus the declared stock, divided by entries.
Flag gap_share above 0.08.

2b.regimes.transit.topic: check that transit movements close, and on time
hints: Goods in transit must come out the other side.
Compute each operator's closure rate and hours against the route norm.
Sort by closure_rate.

2b.regimes.parcels.topic: look for receivers of many parcels each just under the duty-free limit
hints: Many small parcels can be one big shipment.
Count each consignee's parcels per month and their largest value.
consignments at least six and max_value_lcu at least 1,800.

2b.exercise.topic: bin each of the 24 gaps: explained, investigate or needs better data; circle Country A's low chapters
hints: Most gaps have a known explanation.
Apply shipping and insurance, timing and hubs, then read the notes and weight flags before binning.
Investigate only the pairs below 0.80 after shipping, timing and hubs that no note explains; tick a regional chapter only when Country A is below the threshold with the weight coverage to trust.

4b.match.exact.topic: join customs to tax on the tax ID and explain every miss
hints: An exact join misses for different reasons.
Join on the TIN and classify each miss: blank, one character off, or not in the registry.
exact_status = 'TIN one character off'.

4b.match.probable.topic: match on names, address, phone and director when the ID fails, and choose how strict to be
hints: Looser matching finds more and gets more wrong.
Score name similarity plus bonuses for shared address, phone and director; move the threshold.
Compare found and wrong at 95, 85 and 70.

4b.match.trackB.topic: match the customs importer file to a real register; show the weights the data gave you, the dial you chose and why, and the three pairs you are least sure of
hints: Clean both sides the same way.
A missing field is not a zero.
The sample sets the dial, not the weights.

4b.buckets.topic: sort each importer into unregistered, not filing, under-reporting or consistent
hints: Each bucket calls for a different agency.
Check registration, then missing returns, then sales against imports times the sector mark-up.
sales below imports times 1.25 means under-reporting; two missing returns in the last six means not filing.

4b.network.borrowed_names.topic: find tax IDs that several importers share at one address
hints: A name can be borrowed.
Count importers per TIN and address; look at shared brokers, phones and directors.
Group importers by tin and address_line; six or more; read the broker and the lender's returns.

4b.patterns.split_parcels.topic: many parcels just under the limit
hints: Small parcels can add up.
Count parcels per consignee per month near the limit.
consignments at least six, max near the limit.

4b.patterns.land_border.topic: compare home imports at each crossing with the neighbour's exports through it
hints: The neighbour counts the same trucks.
Divide home imports by the neighbour's exports, crossing by crossing, month by month.
Plot the ratio by crossing and month, and fit a trend for each crossing.

4b.patterns.cash_sector.topic: find the sector where many importers declare sales below their imports
hints: Some sectors deal in cash.
Per sector, count importers whose declared sales are below imports.
Cosmetics and personal care stands out.

4b.patterns.origin_washing.topic: preference claims from origins that do not make the goods, through one seller
hints: A hub can relabel origin.
Flag preference claims from non-producing origins and group by seller.
Group doubtful claims by exporter_id.

4b.patterns.borrowed_names.topic: one TIN, many importers, one address
hints: Count who clears under whose number.
Group importers by TIN and address.
Six or more importers at one address.

4b.exercise.topic: track A: bucket each of the 25 importers, choose the action and the lead, find the two networks; track B: match the real register and set the dial
hints: Start from what the registry and the returns say.
Match, then registration, filing, and sales against imports; then look at shared addresses and brokers.
Under-reporting includes the two lenders and the one-digit TIN trap.
